page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with the verse set off as a block. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Two short notes in the right margin, beside the verse. Catchword at lower right, signature at lower left.

main_text.p: tribuuntur virtutum nomina. Ideo Psaltes scaphum scapham appellans, superbiā, violentiam, pinguem aqualiculum, abusum Dei donorum, mores dissolutos, calumniā dilicentiam, temeritate pronunciandi de rebus diuinis & humanis, eis rectè tribuit.
Deinde committit paralogismum τὸ πρὸ[?] τὸ μὴ αἴτιον ὡς αἴτιον, quisquis ex vitiorum effectis colligit felicitatem hoc dignam nomine.
main_text.head: VERSVS X. XI. XII.

p.i: Propterea huc se conuertit populus eius, quoniam aquae pleni calices exprimuntur illis. Et dicunt: Quomodo intelligeret Deus? & an est scientia in excelso? Ecce sunt impij & felices saeculi, & amplificant diuitias.

main_text.p: Differit in his tribus versibus Propheta noster, de Apostatis, hoc est, de iis, qui pondere & diuturnitate rerum aduersarum, & persequutionum ob professionem veritatis, fracti & debilitati, tandem filijs huius saeculi se adiungunt, & eorum sectantur studia.
Docendi autem gratia tria capita, defectionis istius, finitionem, causam, defensionem, ordine exponemus.

page.notes: Page number "147" is partly worn; read as 147. The Greek phrase in the Deinde line is hard to read; the first word is uncertain and marked [?]. The two right-margin notes are faint; "Leu. 4." and "11. Maij." are uncertain. The line-end "il / is" is printed as two lines in the scan and is given as "illis" without a printed hyphen. No hyphen is clearly visible at "pon / dere" and is not added.
